newsitem.title: UK: U.S. firms may face big tax bill under UK's Labour.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firms may face big tax bill under UK's Labour.

text.p: A new study shows U.S. companies may end up footing the lion's share of the bill for the windfall levy on utilities planned by a future British Labour government, the Sunday Times reported.

The newspaper said analysts at broking house NatWest Securities had calculated that U.S. utilities at the forefront of the buying frenzy in the electricity sector last year could face a bill of 1.5 billion stg if Labour accepted a cut-off date of March 1996 for assessing windfall-tax liability.

"Labour might be intrigued to note that delaying the cut-off until then captures more electricity takeovers and almost doubles the burden on predators that are not listed in the UK," NatWest's Adam Forsyth was quoted as saying.
"This could be attractive for Labour, seeking to play down the impact of the levy on UK pension funds."

The latest opinion poll published on Monday showed the opposition Labour Party's lead ahead of the May 1 general election had slipped by three points at the weekend to 16 points over the ruling Conservatives.
